cards.text: Two short songs today, friend, and both are songs of ascents. The first one is by David, Israel's king (2 Samuel 5:3), and he opens with 'Behold,' which is Bible for EVERYBODY LOOK AT THIS. He's found something good and pleasant, and he wants the whole room to see it.

cards.question: What does David say is so good and pleasant?

answers.text: Brothers singing on the road together

cards.text: Then David paints a picture. Fine oil, poured on somebody's head and running down onto his beard.

cards.question: In David's picture, the fine oil runs down ___'s beard.

cards.text: Aaron, Moses' brother, the man God chose to serve Him as priest (Exodus 28:1). And take it from the stamper with the biggest mustache in the Dorinverse: once something lands up top, it is GOING places.

cards.question: In David's picture, how far does the oil run down Aaron?

answers.text: Over the collar of his robes
All the way down to his feet
Onto the floor of the tent

cards.question: True or false: David uses the oil running down Aaron's beard to show how good it is when brothers live together in harmony.

cards.text: And David's not done. This man does NOT do one picture when he can do two. Picture number two: the dew of Hermon, falling.

cards.question: David pictures the dew of Hermon falling on the mountains of ___.

cards.text: Then David drops the big line, nice and easy. There, he says, the LORD has bestowed a blessing.

cards.question: What blessing does David say the LORD has bestowed there?

answers.text: A crown that will never fade

cards.text: Now the second song, another song of ascents, and it's even shorter. It calls out to all the servants of the LORD who serve in the house of the LORD.

cards.question: When do these servants of the LORD serve in His house?

cards.text: The NIGHT SHIFT. Respect. I pulled years of night shift in a junk drawer, and my only coworkers were dead batteries. This song calls these servants to come and bless the LORD.

cards.question: As they bless the LORD, what does the song tell these night servants to do with their hands?

answers.text: Lift them up to the sanctuary

cards.text: Then comes the last line, spoken to those servants. It calls the LORD the Maker of heaven and earth. Friend, I've got one little cookie planet, and I didn't even make THAT.

cards.question: True or false: In the last line, the servants are told to bless the LORD one more time.
The song ends asking that the LORD, the Maker of heaven and earth, bless these servants from ___.

findings.problem: The card says both songs are songs of ascents. That uses Psalm 134:1, but the card cites only Psalm 133:1.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.
Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The question asks 'What blessing.' Only the right answer starts with 'The blessing of…', so it stands out from the two wrong answers.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: The story card has 4 sentences: 'The NIGHT SHIFT.', 'Respect.', the drawer joke, and the call to bless the LORD.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke's action doesn't match. The night servants are actively serving, but Papa Dorin was lying unused in the drawer. Calling that 'night shift' gives the comparison a different action.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: 'My only coworkers were dead batteries' changes his backstory. The drawer also held rubber bands, a twist tie, a birthday candle, a coupon, a mystery key and later a can opener.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: The card says the last line is 'spoken to those servants.' Psalm 134:3 says only 'bless you' and never says who 'you' is.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.
Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The statement treats the servants as the ones addressed in the last line ('the servants are told'). Psalm 134:3 doesn't say who 'you' is.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The question says the LORD is asked to bless 'these servants.' Psalm 134:3 says only 'bless you' and never says who 'you' is.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Half of the 10 choice cards can't be reasoned out from earlier cards: Aaron (card 4), the collar of his robes (card 6), Zion (card 9), life forevermore (card 11) and by night (card 13). Discovery questions should be only a few, with most choice cards being informed guesses.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.
